summary: A one-column developer demo of IBM Plex Sans KR: the name, one Korean word, and the same Yun Dong-ju poem repeated in each of the eight weights (Thin 100 to Bold 700, with a 450 Text weight), plus a light/dark toggle and two source links. It is a weight check sheet more than a microsite.

instances.look: Top of the column stands in for a hero: 'IBM Plex Sans KR' in 54px Bold, the Korean word '혁신하다' (to innovate) in grey Bold below, and a 48px sun icon button at the right that toggles dark mode

A 700px column of eight sections, each a weight label ('Thin (100)', 'ExtraLight (200)' … 'Text (450)' … 'Bold (700)') above the same five-line Korean poem paragraph in that weight, from barely-there grey to dense black
instances.ux: Scroll to compare colour of text across weights; the sun button switches the page to dark mode
instances.learn: Repeat one real text (a known poem) in every weight, labelled with name and numeric weight, so the visitor judges texture rather than letter shapes; a dark-mode toggle doubles the test

reconstruction.layout: Centred column 700px wide (x=370) on a full-page #f4f4f4 ground; header at y≈176; then 8 stacked sections ~188px each: h2 label, 16px gap, paragraph of 5 lines; ~30px between sections; dark-mode button 48×48 top-right of the column
reconstruction.typography: h1 54px IBM Plex Sans Bold, #161616; subheader ~20px IBM Plex Sans KR Bold grey; labels ~20px IBM Plex Sans Regular; paragraphs ~15px IBM Plex Sans KR at font-weight 100, 200, 300, 400, 450, 500, 600, 700 (inline style per p), leading ~1.6, lang=ko
reconstruction.behaviour: Button .dark-mode-toggle swaps the page to light text on dark; no animation
reconstruction.content: Yun Dong-ju's poem '소년' (Boy), the same full paragraph in each weight; heading word '혁신하다'
reconstruction.html: main > button.dark-mode-toggle + div.stack > h1, span.subheader[lang=ko], (h2 + p[lang=ko][style=font-weight:N]) × 8

instances.look: Two small underlined links at the column edges: 'Poem source' left (the poet's archive) and 'Code source' right (GitHub)
